claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a close derivative with conventional grain sizes above 100 nm has a coercive field near 100 Oe.
Severe plastic deformation or rapid consolidation can produce grain sizes below 100 nm in single-phase fcc FeCoNi.
The proposed processing can retain the single-phase fcc structure.
Reducing the grain size below 100 nm increases grain-boundary density and the density of other nanoscale defects.
The increased grain-boundary density provides effective pinning sites for magnetic domain walls.
Grain boundaries and nanoscale defects hinder domain-wall motion.
Hindered domain-wall motion raises the coercive field.
A nanocrystalline microstructure with grain sizes well below 100 nm will significantly increase the coercive field of single-phase fcc FeCoNi.
The coercive field will increase beyond 100 Oe and could reach several hundred Oe.
The nanocrystalline material will retain a high saturation magnetization comparable to that of the untreated single-phase alloy.
The proposed coercivity mechanism applies under room-temperature measurement conditions in which domain-wall motion dominates coercivity.
The intervention is applicable to FeCoNi-derived high-entropy alloys maintained as single-phase fcc materials.
The magnitude of coercivity enhancement may depend on the processing technique.
Excessive processing may introduce defects that reduce saturation magnetization.
